chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'The example of salat is like the example of the central pole of a tent: when the pole stands firm, the ropes and the pegs and the covering are of benefit; and when the pole breaks, neither a rope nor a peg nor a covering is of any benefit.'

key_terms.الأطناب: Tent ropes — the guy-ropes that hold the tent stable
key_terms.الأوتاد: Pegs/stakes — the ground anchors that secure the tent
key_terms.الصلاة: Salat — the ritual prayer, the second pillar of Islam and the most central act of worship
key_terms.الغشاء: Covering — the canopy/fabric of the tent
key_terms.عمود الفسطاط: The central pole of the tent — the keystone of the tent's structure

ai.seo_question: What is the importance of salat (prayer) in Islam according to hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a prophetic saying in which the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) uses the vivid metaphor of a tent to describe the centrality of salat in a believer's religious life. Just as a tent's central pole holds everything together — making ropes, pegs, and the canopy functional — salat is the pillar that gives all other deeds their worth. Without salat, no other act of worship or virtue can stand. This simile, drawn from the familiar nomadic life of Arabia, spoke directly to the Prophet's audience, for whom the tent was a symbol of shelter, order, and the entire fabric of domestic life.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Hamza Bin Humran, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘An example of the Salāt is like an example of the pillars of the tent. When the pillars are firm, the ropes and the pegs and the covering would be of benefit; and when the pillars break, neither the ropes, nor the pegs, nor the covering would be of (any) benefit’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Hamzah ibn Humran from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah from abu ‘Abd Allah, who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Salah (prayer) is like the poles of a tent. If the poles are established then the ropes, pegs and the covering work, but if the poles break, none of the ropes, pegs and covering work.
